title: GDPR Compliance for Programmatic Advertising
content: This document outlines GDPR compliance requirements for programmatic advertising operations. Key requirements: 1) Explicit consent must be obtained before processing personal data for ad targeting. 2) Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) must be in place with all demand-side and supply-side partners. 3) Right to erasure requests must be processed within 72 hours across all targeting segments. 4) Data retention for audience profiles must not exceed 13 months without renewed consent. 5) Cross-border data transfers require Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or adequacy decisions. Impact on operations: all audience segments using PII-derived signals must be flagged and consent-verified before bid submission. Non-compliant segments must be excluded from bid requests in EU/EEA inventory.

title: Brand Safety Guidelines v3.2
content: FlexAd Brand Safety Policy. Tier 1 (Block All Clients): adult content, illegal activity, hate speech, terrorism, weapons, drugs. Tier 2 (Block by Default, Override Available): political content, gambling, alcohol, tobacco, controversial news. Tier 3 (Client-Configurable): user-generated content, gaming violence, celebrity gossip, sensitive social topics. Implementation: Pre-bid blocking via IAS/DV integration. Post-bid monitoring with 24-hour incident response. Monthly brand safety audit of top 100 domains by spend. Escalation path: Tier 1 violations → immediate block + client notification within 1 hour. Tier 2 → block within 4 hours + weekly report. Tier 3 → flag in dashboard + monthly review.

title: Invalid Traffic (IVT) Detection and Prevention
content: FlexAd IVT Prevention Framework. Detection methods: 1) Pre-bid filters using IP reputation databases, device fingerprinting, and behavioral analysis. 2) Post-bid verification via DoubleVerify and IAS pixel monitoring. 3) Internal ML model scoring bid requests on 47 features including request timing patterns, geographic consistency, device-session correlation, and click-to-conversion timing. Classification: GIVT (General Invalid Traffic) — bots, crawlers, known data centers — automatically filtered pre-bid. SIVT (Sophisticated Invalid Traffic) — ad stacking, pixel stuffing, domain spoofing, cookie manipulation — detected via behavioral ML models with 4-hour lag. Thresholds: Any campaign exceeding 5% SIVT rate triggers automatic investigation. Campaigns above 10% IVT are paused and refunds issued within 48 hours.

title: RTB Bid Strategy Best Practices
content: Real-Time Bidding optimization guide for campaign managers. Bid strategies: 1) Target CPA — set desired cost per acquisition, algorithm adjusts bids to achieve target. Best for: conversion campaigns with stable historical data. 2) Maximize Conversions — spend full budget while maximizing conversion volume. Best for: campaigns in learning phase or with flexible CPA targets. 3) Target ROAS — optimize bids to achieve target return on ad spend. Best for: e-commerce campaigns with revenue tracking. 4) Manual CPM — fixed bid price per 1000 impressions. Best for: brand awareness campaigns. Bid modifiers: Time of day (+/- 30%), device type (+/- 50%), audience segment (+/- 100%), viewability score (+/- 25%). Pacing: Even pacing distributes spend uniformly. Front-loaded pacing spends 60% in first half. ASAP pacing bids maximum until budget depletes. Recommended: Even pacing for most campaigns; ASAP only for flash sales or limited-time promotions.

title: CCPA and US State Privacy Law Compliance
content: Compliance framework for US state privacy laws including CCPA/CPRA (California), CPA (Colorado), CTDPA (Connecticut), UCPA (Utah), and VCDPA (Virginia). Key obligations: 1) Honor opt-out signals — Global Privacy Control (GPC) must be detected and respected within bid requests. 2) Do Not Sell/Share — maintain a universal opt-out list synchronized across all DSP partners within 15 business days. 3) Sensitive data categories (precise geolocation, health, financial, race/ethnicity) require explicit opt-in consent in CA, CO, CT. 4) Data minimization — collect only data necessary for the stated advertising purpose. Implementation: US Privacy String signals in bid requests must be parsed and respected. Consent Management Platform (CMP) integration required for all publisher-side inventory.

title: Creative Specification Standards
content: FlexAd Creative Specifications. Display: 300x250 (Medium Rectangle) — max 150KB, HTML5 or static image. 728x90 (Leaderboard) — max 150KB. 160x600 (Wide Skyscraper) — max 150KB. 320x50 (Mobile Banner) — max 100KB. All display: max 15s animation, must have clickTag implemented, SSL required. Video: Pre-roll 15s/30s — max 100MB, MP4/WebM, 1920x1080 or 1280x720, 24-30fps, max 10Mbps bitrate. CTV: 15s/30s/60s — VAST 4.2 compliant, 1920x1080, companion banner required. Audio: 15s/30s — max 5MB, MP3/OGG, 128kbps minimum. Native: Headline max 25 chars, body max 90 chars, image 1200x627 minimum. All formats must pass LEAN (Light, Encrypted, Ad-choice supported, Non-invasive) standards. Third-party tracking pixels limited to 3 per creative.

title: Viewability Standards and Measurement
content: FlexAd viewability measurement standards aligned with MRC/IAB guidelines. Display viewability: 50% of pixels in-view for 1 continuous second. Video viewability: 50% of pixels in-view for 2 continuous seconds with audio on or user-initiated. Large format display (242,500+ pixels): 30% of pixels in-view for 1 continuous second. Measurement partners: DoubleVerify (primary), IAS (secondary). Viewability targets by channel: Display — 70% minimum, Video — 65% minimum, Native — 75% minimum, CTV — 95% expected. Low-viewability remediation: Placements below 40% viewability for 3 consecutive days → automatic block. Placements between 40-60% → bid reduction of 30%. Monthly viewability audit across top 500 publisher domains.

title: Audience Data Management and Segmentation
content: FlexAd audience data management policies. Data sources: 1st party (advertiser CRM, pixel data, conversion events), 2nd party (publisher data partnerships), 3rd party (data marketplace providers). Segment creation rules: Minimum segment size — 10,000 unique users for targeting. Maximum segment age — 90 days without refresh for behavioral segments, 180 days for demographic. Lookalike modeling: Seed audience minimum 1,000 converters, expansion ratio 1:10 to 1:50 based on precision requirements. Data hygiene: Monthly deduplication across all identity graphs. Quarterly audit of third-party segment accuracy via holdout testing. Cookie-to-ID resolution using probabilistic matching (85% confidence threshold) and deterministic matching where available. Privacy-safe clean room processing for advertiser 1P data onboarding.

title: Campaign Launch Checklist
content: Pre-launch checklist for all FlexAd campaigns. Phase 1 — Setup (24h before launch): Verify advertiser contract and IO terms. Confirm budget allocation and pacing strategy. Review targeting parameters (geo, audience, context). Validate creative assets (specs, tracking pixels, landing pages). Set frequency caps and dayparting rules. Phase 2 — QA (12h before launch): Test all tracking pixels fire correctly. Verify conversion events in advertiser's analytics. Run test bid requests through staging environment. Confirm brand safety settings match advertiser tier. Review placement lists (allow/block). Phase 3 — Go Live (first 4 hours): Monitor delivery rate — should reach 10% of daily budget in first 2 hours. Check win rate — should be above 10% for standard campaigns. Verify impression geography matches targeting. Confirm viewability is above 60% threshold. Flag any IVT anomalies above 3%. Phase 4 — Optimization (day 2-7): Adjust bids based on early performance signals. Expand or narrow audience based on engagement. A/B test creative variations. Set up automated rules for pacing and performance alerts.

title: Cross-Device Attribution Methodology
content: FlexAd cross-device attribution framework. Identity resolution: Deterministic matching via login events (email hash, account ID) — 40% of cross-device links. Probabilistic matching via device graph signals (IP, location, browsing patterns) — 60% of cross-device links. Attribution models: Last-touch — default model, 100% credit to final touchpoint. Linear — equal credit distributed across all touchpoints. Time-decay — more recent touchpoints receive proportionally more credit (7-day half-life). Position-based — 40% first touch, 40% last touch, 20% distributed to middle touchpoints. Data-driven — ML model trained on conversion paths, updated weekly. Conversion window: Click-through — 30 days default (configurable 1-90 days). View-through — 1 day default (configurable 1-7 days). Cross-device — 7 days post identity resolution. Deduplication: When multiple devices in a graph convert, credit the device with the highest-confidence identity match.

title: Supply Path Optimization (SPO) Policy
content: FlexAd Supply Path Optimization guidelines. Goal: Reduce bid duplication, lower fees, and improve auction transparency. Evaluation criteria for SSP partners: 1) Auction mechanics — preference for first-price auctions with bid shading. 2) Fee transparency — require disclosed take rates. 3) Header bidding support — unified auction preferred over waterfall. 4) Direct publisher connections — prioritize SSPs with >60% direct supply. 5) ads.txt/sellers.json compliance — mandatory for all partners. Quarterly SPO review process: Analyze bid request duplication across SSPs. Calculate effective CPM after fees for each path. Measure win rate and post-auction discrepancy by SSP. Remove paths with >20% duplication rate or <5% unique inventory. Target: Reduce active SSP connections from current 45 to optimal 15-20. Expected savings: 8-12% reduction in effective CPM through fee elimination.

title: CTV Advertising Best Practices
content: Connected TV advertising guidelines for FlexAd campaigns. Inventory types: OTT streaming services (Hulu, Peacock, Paramount+, Tubi), Smart TV native apps, Gaming console apps, MVPD/vMVPD (YouTube TV, Sling). Targeting capabilities: Household-level targeting (IP-based), ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) data for content context, First-party publisher segments, Cross-screen retargeting (CTV viewer → mobile/display follow-up). Creative requirements: VAST 4.2 compliant, 15s and 30s spots (both required), 1920x1080 HD minimum, Companion banner 300x250 recommended, Server-side ad insertion (SSAI) compatible. Measurement: Completion rate benchmark — 95%+ (non-skippable). Reach and frequency via household graph. Incremental reach vs linear TV using ACR overlap data. Brand lift studies via exposed/control methodology. Performance benchmarks: CPM $20-45, completion rate >95%, household reach 2-5% per campaign.

title: Data Clean Room Implementation Guide
content: FlexAd Data Clean Room operations using Snowflake. Purpose: Enable privacy-safe audience matching between FlexAd and advertiser/publisher first-party data without exposing raw PII. Setup process: 1) Create secure share from advertiser's Snowflake account. 2) Define approved queries in clean room (overlap analysis, lookalike modeling, attribution). 3) Apply differential privacy with epsilon=1.0 for aggregate outputs. 4) Minimum aggregation threshold — k=50 (no group smaller than 50 users returned). Use cases: Audience overlap analysis — measure shared audience between advertiser CRM and FlexAd exposure data. Conversion attribution — match ad exposures to conversions without sharing user-level data. Lookalike seed creation — identify high-value user characteristics in advertiser data, build lookalike in FlexAd graph. Frequency analysis — cross-reference household exposure with purchase data across walled gardens. Governance: All queries require dual approval (FlexAd + data partner). Audit log retained for 3 years. Annual compliance review by external auditor.

title: Programmatic Guaranteed (PG) and Private Marketplace (PMP) Guide
content: Managed deal types at FlexAd. Programmatic Guaranteed (PG): Fixed price, guaranteed volume. Publisher reserves inventory for specific advertiser. Typically premium placements (homepage takeover, first-look video). Minimum commitment: $50K/month. Setup time: 5-7 business days for deal ID creation and QA. Private Marketplace (PMP): Fixed or floor price, non-guaranteed. Curated inventory packages by publisher vertical, audience, or context. Minimum spend: $10K/month. Setup time: 2-3 business days. Preferred Deals: First-look access at negotiated price before open auction. No volume commitment. Ideal for testing publisher quality before PG commitment. Deal troubleshooting: No delivery — check deal ID mapping, creative approval status, bid floor vs bid price. Low win rate — verify targeting alignment with deal terms, check creative format compatibility. Discrepancy >10% — reconcile impression counts with publisher, check for ad server caching issues.

title: Machine Learning Model Governance for Ad Targeting
content: ML model governance framework for FlexAd's targeting and optimization models. Model inventory: 1) Bid prediction model — estimates optimal bid price (updated hourly). 2) CTR prediction model — predicts click probability per impression (updated daily). 3) Conversion prediction model — predicts conversion probability (updated daily). 4) Audience propensity model — scores users for segment membership (updated weekly). 5) IVT detection model — classifies traffic as valid/invalid (real-time). Model review cadence: Monthly performance review (AUC, calibration, feature drift). Quarterly bias audit (demographic fairness across protected groups). Annual full model retraining with expanded feature set. Fairness requirements: Models must not use race, religion, sexual orientation, or health status as features. Proxy feature detection — monitor for features correlated >0.7 with protected attributes. Equal opportunity metric — true positive rate variance <5% across demographic groups. Rollback policy: Any model version with >2% performance degradation vs baseline is automatically rolled back within 1 hour.

title: Reporting and Analytics Standards
content: FlexAd standard reporting definitions and methodology. Core metrics: Impressions — counted when ad is served (served impression) or when viewable (viewable impression, MRC standard). Clicks — counted on user-initiated click, deduplicated within 60-second window. Conversions — counted on server-side postback or pixel fire, deduplicated within attribution window. Spend — actual cleared price in auction (not bid price). Revenue — attributed revenue from conversion events (advertiser-reported). Derived metrics: CTR = Clicks / Impressions. CVR = Conversions / Clicks. CPM = (Spend / Impressions) × 1000. CPC = Spend / Clicks. CPA = Spend / Conversions. ROAS = Revenue / Spend. eCPM = (Revenue / Impressions) × 1000. Reporting cadence: Real-time dashboard — 15-minute data refresh for active campaigns. Daily report — finalized by 6 AM ET following day. Weekly digest — sent Monday AM with prior week performance. Monthly close — finalized by 5th business day, reconciled with billing.

title: Incident Response Plan for Ad Operations
content: FlexAd AdOps incident response playbook. Severity levels: P1 (Critical) — platform-wide delivery failure, data breach, major brand safety incident. Response: immediate war room, 15-minute updates to stakeholders, 1-hour resolution target. P2 (High) — single advertiser delivery failure, IVT spike >15%, attribution pipeline down. Response: 30-minute acknowledgment, 4-hour resolution target. P3 (Medium) — reporting delays, minor creative rendering issues, single SSP connectivity. Response: 2-hour acknowledgment, 24-hour resolution target. P4 (Low) — cosmetic issues, minor discrepancies, feature requests. Response: next business day acknowledgment, 1-week resolution target. Escalation path: On-call engineer → Team lead → VP Engineering → CTO. Communication: P1/P2 — real-time Slack channel + email to affected clients. P3/P4 — ticket update in Jira. Post-incident: All P1/P2 require blameless post-mortem within 48 hours with action items tracked to completion.

title: Contextual Targeting Without Cookies
content: FlexAd's cookieless targeting strategy. Context: Third-party cookie deprecation requires alternative targeting methods. Solutions: 1) Contextual targeting — AI-powered page content analysis using NLP. Categories: IAB Content Taxonomy v3.0 (700+ categories). Sentiment analysis for brand safety. Keyword targeting with negative keyword support. 2) Cohort-based targeting — Privacy Sandbox Topics API integration. Interest-based cohorts without individual tracking. Weekly topic refresh cycle. 3) First-party data activation — Server-side tag management for 1P data collection. Identity resolution via hashed email (SHA-256). Customer data platform (CDP) integration for audience building. 4) Seller-defined audiences (SDA) — Publisher-curated segments based on login data. Premium pricing but higher match rates. 5) Universal IDs — Support for UID2.0, ID5, LiveRamp RampID. Match rates: 40-60% depending on publisher adoption. Performance comparison vs cookies: Contextual — 85% of cookie-based CTR at 70% of CPM. Cohort-based — 75% of cookie-based CTR. 1P data — 110% of cookie-based CTR at 120% of CPM.

title: Retail Media Network Integration
content: FlexAd integration with Retail Media Networks (RMNs). Supported networks: Amazon DSP, Walmart Connect, Target Roundel, Kroger Precision Marketing, Instacart Ads, Best Buy Ads. Integration types: API-based campaign management (preferred), Self-serve UI access (fallback), Server-to-server conversion feed. Key advantages: Closed-loop measurement — connect ad exposure to actual purchase data. High-intent audiences — shoppers actively browsing product categories. First-party data — based on purchase history, not inferred behavior. Integration requirements per RMN: Amazon DSP — API access via Amazon Advertising API, entity management. Walmart Connect — API v3, campaign and reporting endpoints. Kroger — Secure file transfer for audience and measurement data. Reporting unification: All RMN performance data ingested into FlexAd's reporting layer. Cross-channel attribution supports RMN as touchpoint alongside programmatic display/video. Incrementality testing available via geo-based holdout methodology.

title: Sustainability and Carbon Reporting for Digital Advertising
content: FlexAd carbon emission tracking for digital advertising. Methodology: Based on Scope3 framework, measuring carbon emissions per 1000 ad impressions (gCO2PM — grams of CO2 per mille). Emission sources: 1) Ad selection and decisioning — server compute for bid processing. 2) Creative delivery — CDN bandwidth and data transfer. 3) Publisher page load — proportional share of page weight attributable to ads. 4) End-user device energy — proportional display rendering cost. Current baseline: Average gCO2PM across FlexAd campaigns: 1.2g (industry avg: 1.8g). Reduction targets: 20% reduction by end of 2026 (target: 0.96g gCO2PM). Low-carbon optimization: Prefer SSPs with green hosting (renewable energy data centers). Reduce creative file sizes — compress video, optimize image delivery. Implement SPO to reduce redundant bid requests (each wasted request = ~0.1mg CO2). Reporting: Monthly carbon report per campaign available in dashboard. Annual sustainability report for enterprise advertisers. Green Media Product (GMP) certification available for campaigns meeting <0.8g gCO2PM.

title: Attention Metrics and Optimization
content: FlexAd attention measurement framework. Beyond viewability: While viewability measures opportunity to see, attention metrics measure actual user engagement with ad units. Attention signals: 1) Active page time — duration of active browser tab with ad in view. 2) Scroll velocity — slower scroll near ad = higher attention. 3) Mouse proximity — cursor near/over ad creative. 4) Content engagement — time spent on landing page post-click. 5) Audio engagement — for video/audio, unmuted playback duration. Attention score: Composite 0-100 score combining all signals, normalized by ad format and placement. Benchmarks by format: Display — median attention score 22. Video pre-roll — median 58. CTV — median 72. Native — median 35. Audio — median 45. Optimization: Attention-weighted bidding — increase bids on placements with historical attention scores above 50. Reporting: Attention heatmap by publisher domain. Correlation analysis: attention vs conversion rate (typical R²=0.65). Cost per attentive second as efficiency metric.

title: Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA) Implementation
content: FlexAd MTA platform and methodology. Data pipeline: Ad server logs → identity resolution → path construction → model training → credit allocation. Path construction rules: Maximum path length — 90 days. Minimum path length — 1 touchpoint (direct response). Touchpoint types: impression (view), click, site visit, video completion, audio listen. Deduplication window: 60 seconds for duplicate impressions. Model architecture: Shapley value-based attribution using cooperative game theory. Each touchpoint's marginal contribution calculated across all possible coalitions. Updated weekly with rolling 90-day training window. Validation: Holdout group (5% of traffic) for incremental lift measurement. Monthly calibration check — MTA-predicted conversions within 5% of actual. A/B test alignment — MTA credit allocation should directionally match A/B test results for +/- 10% campaigns. Output: Channel-level credit allocation with confidence intervals. Publisher-level ROAS rankings. Optimal budget allocation recommendation (constrained optimization). Path-to-conversion analysis — most common conversion paths by advertiser vertical.

title: Ad Personalization and Dynamic Creative Optimization (DCO)
content: FlexAd DCO framework. Dynamic Creative Optimization automatically assembles ad creatives from component parts based on user context. Components: Headline variations (5-10 per campaign). Body copy variations (3-5). Product images (from feed). CTAs (2-3 options). Background colors/themes (2-4). Layout templates (2-3). Decisioning signals: User segment membership. Geographic location (city-level). Weather conditions (for weather-triggered campaigns). Time of day/day of week. Device type and screen size. Previous ad exposure and engagement history. Optimization algorithm: Multi-armed bandit (Thompson Sampling) for component selection. Exploration phase: first 10,000 impressions per combination. Exploitation phase: converge on top-performing combinations. Continuous learning: 10% exploration budget maintained throughout campaign. Performance lift: Average CTR improvement: +25-40% vs static creative. Average CVR improvement: +15-30% vs static creative. Setup time: 3-5 business days for feed integration and template creation.

title: Header Bidding and Auction Mechanics
content: FlexAd participation in header bidding auctions. Header bidding overview: Publishers run simultaneous auctions across multiple SSPs before their ad server decides. This gives FlexAd equal access to premium inventory alongside other DSPs. Prebid.js integration: FlexAd adapter available in Prebid.js v8.x+. Configuration: timeout 1500ms, bidder code 'flexad'. Server-to-server (S2S): Lower latency, handled by Prebid Server. Recommended for mobile and CTV. Auction dynamics: First-price auction — FlexAd bids its true willingness to pay (adjusted by bid shading algorithm). Bid shading: ML model predicts clearing price based on historical data (publisher, format, time, audience). Average savings from bid shading: 15-25% vs naive first-price bids. Floors: Publisher-set floor prices respected. Dynamic floors (varying by time/audience) handled automatically. Header bidding analytics: Win rate by publisher/format. Timeout rate (bids not returned in time). Bid-to-impression ratio. Revenue per impression vs open auction.

title: Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) Roadmap
content: FlexAd PET adoption roadmap. Current (2025): Differential privacy for aggregate reporting (epsilon=1.0). K-anonymity enforcement (k=50) in all audience exports. Hashed identifiers (SHA-256) for all PII in transit and at rest. TLS 1.3 for all API communications. Near-term (2026): On-device processing for frequency capping (no server-side user tracking). Trusted Execution Environments (TEE) for cross-party computation. Secure multi-party computation (MPC) for attribution with publishers. Federated learning for audience model training without centralizing data. Medium-term (2027): Homomorphic encryption for encrypted bid evaluation. Zero-knowledge proofs for audience qualification without revealing segment membership. Private Information Retrieval (PIR) for ad serving without revealing user identity to SSP. Privacy budget management across all data operations. Impact assessment: PET adoption increases compute costs by estimated 15-30%. Targeting efficiency may decrease 5-10% but compliance risk reduced by >90%. Competitive advantage: early PET adoption positions FlexAd for post-cookie regulatory landscape.

title: Video Advertising Completion Rate Optimization
content: Strategies for improving video ad completion rates. Current benchmarks: 15s pre-roll — 88% completion. 30s pre-roll — 72% completion. 15s mid-roll — 92% completion. 30s mid-roll — 85% completion. CTV all formats — 96% completion. Optimization levers: 1) Creative quality — first 3 seconds critical for retention. Test multiple openings. Brand placement: early (0-5s) vs late (last 5s). 2) Placement selection — mid-roll consistently outperforms pre-roll by 10-15%. Content-aligned placements improve completion by 8%. 3) Targeting — retargeting audiences complete 12% more than prospecting. High-intent segments complete 18% more than broad targeting. 4) Frequency — completion rate drops 5% after 3rd exposure, 15% after 5th. 5) Device — CTV has highest completion (non-skippable environment). Mobile completion lowest but highest conversion intent. Measurement: VAST events tracked: start, firstQuartile, midpoint, thirdQuartile, complete. Video viewability = 50% pixels + 2s continuous + audio on. VTR (View-Through Rate) = completions / impressions.

title: Ad Fraud Prevention — Advanced Techniques
content: Advanced ad fraud detection and prevention at FlexAd. Sophisticated Invalid Traffic (SIVT) types: 1) Domain spoofing — fraudulent sellers misrepresent domain. Detection: ads.txt/sellers.json cross-reference, domain verification via cryptographic signatures (ads.cert). 2) Ad stacking — multiple ads layered on single placement. Detection: viewability measurement, z-index analysis via verification SDK. 3) Pixel stuffing — ads rendered in 1x1 pixel iframe. Detection: creative rendering verification, impression-to-viewable ratio analysis. 4) Click injection (mobile) — malware triggers clicks before legitimate app install. Detection: click-to-install timing analysis (CTIT), referrer validation. 5) SDK spoofing — fake SDK traffic mimicking real app activity. Detection: cryptographic SDK verification, behavioral pattern analysis. ML detection model: 47 features including timing entropy, geographic consistency, device fingerprint stability, session depth, conversion path plausibility. Updated hourly. False positive rate: <0.1%. Detection rate: >98% for known SIVT patterns, >85% for novel patterns. Financial impact: Estimated $2.3M in fraud prevented monthly across all campaigns.

title: Advertiser Onboarding Playbook
content: Standard onboarding process for new FlexAd advertisers. Week 1 — Discovery: Understand business objectives, KPIs, and success metrics. Audit existing digital advertising setup. Review historical performance data. Identify target audiences and competitive landscape. Week 2 — Setup: Create advertiser account and billing configuration. Implement tracking pixels (site-wide, conversion events, audience). Set up data feeds for dynamic creative (product catalogs). Configure brand safety settings per advertiser tier. Week 3 — Campaign Architecture: Design campaign structure (objectives → campaigns → ad groups → creatives). Build audience segments (1P data onboarding + 3P enrichment). Create initial creative assets and get approval. Set up A/B testing framework for creative and targeting. Week 4 — Launch and Optimize: Launch campaigns with conservative budgets (50% of target). Monitor first 48-hour performance hourly. Adjust bids, targeting, and creative based on early signals. Ramp to full budget by end of week 4 if performance meets thresholds. Success criteria for onboarding completion: All tracking validated and firing correctly. At least 2 campaigns live and delivering. First optimization cycle completed. Weekly reporting cadence established.

title: Audience Suppression and Negative Targeting
content: Audience suppression best practices. Purpose: Exclude specific users from campaign targeting to improve efficiency and compliance. Common suppression use cases: 1) Existing customer suppression — exclude users who already purchased/subscribed. Reduces wasted spend by 15-25% for acquisition campaigns. 2) Frequency cap enforcement — suppress users who reached max frequency across campaigns. 3) Competitor employee suppression — exclude known competitor company IPs and domains. 4) Compliance suppression — exclude users who opted out or requested data deletion. Must be applied within 72 hours of request. 5) Negative conversion suppression — exclude users who returned products or cancelled subscriptions. Implementation: CRM list upload (hashed email/phone). Real-time suppression via server-side cookie sync. Segment-based suppression in DSP. IP-range suppression for geo/company targeting. Best practices: Refresh suppression lists daily for CRM-based exclusions. Apply suppression before bid to save on bid costs (not just post-bid filtering). Monitor suppression overlap — if >30% of target audience is suppressed, review targeting strategy. Track suppression impact: compare CPA/ROAS with and without suppression active.

title: Measurement Lift Studies and Incrementality
content: FlexAd incrementality measurement methodology. Purpose: Determine the true causal impact of advertising beyond what would have happened organically. Study types: 1) Geo-based lift study — randomly assign geographic regions to test (ads shown) and control (ads withheld). Duration: 4-8 weeks minimum. Minimum markets: 20 test + 20 control. Statistical method: difference-in-differences with propensity score matching. 2) Ghost bid study — in real-time auction, randomly designate some won auctions as control (ad served but tracked as if not). Advantages: user-level randomization, faster results. Disadvantages: requires ad serving platform integration. 3) Conversion lift study (platform-specific) — partner with walled gardens (Meta, Google, Amazon) using their built-in lift study tools. Uses platform's identity graph for randomization. Statistical requirements: Minimum detectable effect: 5% lift. Confidence level: 95% (p<0.05). Statistical power: 80%. Minimum sample size varies by vertical (typically 100K+ exposures in test group). Reporting: Incremental conversions = total conversions × (1 - 1/lift). Incremental ROAS = incremental revenue / total spend. Cost per incremental conversion. Lift by segment/channel/creative for optimization.
